events.label: Jess and friends sail into storm
events.description: Jess, a worn-down mother with a disabled son, joins friends on a yacht trip - and the weekend runs into a ferocious storm that capsizes the boat.

events.label: Board deserted ocean liner Aeolus
events.description: Clinging to the hull, the survivors are picked up by an enormous deserted ocean liner - the Aeolus - drifting silently in the grey.

events.label: Masked shooter attacks the party
events.description: Aboard the empty liner, someone in a sackcloth mask hunts them through the corridors, killing the party one by one.

events.label: Jess realizes she is looping; seagulls/repeats
events.description: Jess starts noticing the film's seams: piles of her own discarded jackets, a trail of identical lockets, dead gulls in the same spot - she has been on this ship before, many times.

events.label: Jess kills versions of friends to 'reset'
events.description: Working out that the ship resets, Jess turns executioner - killing the other versions of herself and her friends to steer the loop toward a version where she can get home.

events.label: Jess becomes the masked killer for next iteration
events.description: The loop's punchline: wounded, stripped of everything, she puts on the mask herself and becomes the killer who hunts the next group of survivors coming aboard.

events.label: Survives wreck; returns home
events.description: The ship's cycle breaks and Jess washes ashore - back in the city, ahead of the storm, with one chance to stop the yacht ever leaving.

events.label: Finds double at home; kills her and takes place
events.description: She reaches home in time to see herself - the Jess who stayed - abusing her son; she kills her double and takes her place, choosing the loop's door again.

events.label: Hitches to harbor to restart sailing trip
events.description: The film ends where it began: Jess, driving to the harbour to board the yacht - the whole tragedy lining up to happen again.

events.label: Grief over disabled son fuels the loop
events.description: Underneath every reset is the same wound: her son, autistic and demanding, and the mother whose exhaustion and guilt the loop turns into a machine.

events.label: Ship Aeolus — circular wandering / wind god
events.description: The ship's name is the key: Aeolus, the keeper of the winds - the father of the Sisyphus the myth condemns to roll his stone forever.

events.label: Loop continues; no external exit shown
events.description: No version of the story shows the way out - the loop has no external exit, only roles that rotate: victim, killer, witness.

events.label: Yachtsmen find deserted liner
events.description: The yacht survivors who find the silent liner are the loop's raw material.

events.label: Aeolus loop of murders
events.description: Aboard the Aeolus, the murders repeat in exact sequence - a script the ship performs on every pass.

events.label: Jess iterations try to break
events.description: Every iteration of Jess reaches the same crossroads - flee, fight, or become.

events.label: Forced killings to 'save' son
events.description: The killings the loop forces: each Jess kills to save her son, and damns the next pass.

events.label: Shore / taxi returns to start
events.description: The taxi driver who takes Jess to the harbour - a silent figure who has made this journey with her before.

events.label: Car crash resets emotional loop
events.description: The car crash at the story's hinge - the accident that kills the child and makes the loop personal.

events.label: Closed narrative loop
events.description: The ship's grammar: die aboard and wake at the mooring; leave the ship and the world outside keeps its own, crueler count.

events.label: Guilt as engine
events.description: The engine of the whole loop: a mother's guilt, turned into a ship that never lets her finish paying it.

ruleEffects.effect: Attempts to reset by murder fulfill the next loop's attacker role
Apparent home escape only reloads the harbor departure

outcome.summary: Jess is trapped in identity-replacement murder loop aboard Aeolus; grief locks the cycle.
